headline: A paper models GPU energy per output token from active bytes and decode time
summary: A new arXiv paper proposes a compact model for GPU-board energy per output token during dense, full-history LLM decoding. The model combines logical weight and KV-cache bytes per output with observed decode time, using coefficients calibrated separately for each model and hardware/runtime configuration. Across three BF16 models on GH200 and GB300 GPUs, plus a two-GH200 tensor-parallel setup, the authors report held-out condition-mean estimates within 3.73% of measured board energy across 270 executions and 54 static conditions. In the tested ranges, larger batches use less mean board energy per useful output, while longer histories increase it. These author-reported fits are configuration-specific; independent reproduction, facility energy and monetary savings are not established.
